steps.text: Someplace in the wilderness, Kazdel

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: ...Hah.

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: Haha! Hahahaha!

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: Prophecy? As if this could be called prophecy! Ascalon did NOT kill me!

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: What has been spoken still requires discernment, what has been discerned can still be altered. The essence of prophetic Arts is merely conjecture and calculation. No wonder there is no destiny that can't be defied!

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: The Cyclops Court is nothing more than a big, sick joke!

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: *spit* That hurts.

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: I didn't die under Ascalon's blade. This isn't what I prophesized...

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: Then maybe she's the one who should've died.

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: She's bound to come confirm that I'm dead. When that happens, you lot can nail down her shadow and rip her to shreds.

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: She's wounded too. I didn't get all beaten up for nothing after all...

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: What are you guys doing?

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: You're aiming at me? Really?

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: Who bought you off?

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: Nobody, boss.

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: It's just a good opportunity to get a promotion.

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: An opportunity? I see. Babel's entered the city, and you could take my head to curry favor with them.

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: If Babel loses, you can always go back to the Scar Market. Nothing to lose.
Scareye silently looks at the soldiers he set up for the ambush himself.
The wind sweeps past, carrying the faint scent of his blood.

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: Heh.

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: It's a good plan, fellas.
Fate did not kill him. He made it. He had reversed a prophecy.
And then he died atop a stage of his own making.
Londinium, Victoria
The huge palace complex situated in the center of Londinium is always too quiet.
Theresis disdains the apathetic nobles who live within. He only respects those who put their lives on the line to fight a way out and come up to him.
Even if the swords that they raise are pointed at Theresis himself—

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Showing mercy to your enemy will only result in your own death, Manfred. Do not repeat that mistake again.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Forgive me, General. I thought—

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Focus on the enemy. It seems these traitors have been sharpening their blades for this ambush for a while now.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: They have stirred the hearts of the Victorians. We are the only ones who can extinguish this rebellion now.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: *Ancient Sarkaz Language*—
By the time he murmurs his covert orders, a group of silent figures are already appearing on the chaotic battlefield.
Like a passing gale rattling the raindrops in a storm.

steps.name: Name-Forsaken Sacrificer
steps.text: Stand back.

steps.name: Babel Assassin
steps.text: Hmph. We'll handle these guys.

steps.name: Babel Assassin
steps.text: Julie, you and the rest keep going.

steps.name: Julie
steps.text: Got it.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Don't even think of getting close to the General.

steps.name: Julie
steps.text: No need to rush. It'll be your turn soon.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: I am the General's guard captain, assassin.

steps.name: Julie
steps.text: Then you're gonna wanna hold your sword tight.
An inconspicuous arc sweeps past Julie's eyes.
A chill runs through her spine. Her body stiffens.
She thinks of the day that she saw Her Highness in the Scar Market.
At the time, she did not even dare to raise her sword.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Enough, Manfred.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: General!

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: They have come to me in search of an honorable death, not mercy.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: They are using their lives to show me the future as they see it.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: You are in a race. She is facing countless threats in Kazdel, just as we are here.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Such a race only ends with my life, or hers.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: I will give you a chance. Come, deathmongers. Kill me. Do not disappoint Theresa.

a.text: Countdown
2 hours, 7 minutes, 21 seconds

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: 'SHATTER'.

steps.name: Panicked Royal Court Soldier
steps.text: Th-The gates have fallen! They're about to come through!

a.text: Countdown
1 hour, 33 minutes, 48 seconds

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Notify all operations within the city to disarm the patrolling troops.

steps.name: Ace
steps.text: The defenses in the city are weak. It's pretty much just the Military Commission's defense forces.

steps.name: Ace
steps.text: We'll strike at them before they can regroup. Move fast.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Even if both sides are trying to prevent the battle from spreading into the city, this is still rather irregular.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Send all our intelligence back to the Doctor. All operating teams, quicken your pace, and stay vigilant at all times.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Take down the Military Commission's flag in the plaza, and tune our radio into all frequencies in the city.

a.text: Countdown
49 minutes, 59 seconds

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Prepare for the landship's connection. We want to let Her Highness and the others enter the region that we control ASAP.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Also contact Ascalon's team and tell them to rendezvous quickly. Three teams have already completed their deployments ahead of schedule.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: Where to next, Dr. Kal'tsit?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The former site of Babel.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Babel's flag has not been raised there for many years.
Kal'tsit walks along the street. She's still familiar with the route to Babel's offices.
The Sarkaz on the street quietly move about, climbing as high as they can on the surrounding buildings, gazing at the same ruins within the city.
A flag that has not been seen in Kazdel for many years slowly rises.
Babel has returned.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Mantra's latest report says we've managed to completely clear five main roads.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: If everything is going according to plan, Kal'tsit should have seen the fires of the Soul Furnace by now.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Kazdel's defenses are all but crippled, Doctor. We can board the city now.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Good.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: But the Military Commission will not give up on Kazdel. If we want complete control of the city, we still need a bit more time.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: By then, we might not be able to completely avert the destruction of Kazdel's center city—

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Wait.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: I felt them.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: They are still here, but they have no intention of aiding anyone.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: It seems that some arrogant bystanders have joined our battle.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Theresa.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Hmm...

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: I also feel... enemies. Not ordinary ones.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Their souls burn with killing intent, sorrow, misery and determination.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: The Military Commission's assassins. They intended to use the city as bait all along, so they can inflict heavy damage on Babel's headquarters.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: This was also within my calculations. But this time, there is no wagering or planning our way out of this. We must defeat the assassins, then return to our city.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: I will go control the landship's defense systems and mount a defense.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Go, Doctor.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: We need not bring another fight into the city, not as it bathes in the twilight afterglow.

a.text: Countdown
22 minutes, 48 seconds

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Closure, have you made contact with the landship?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Still no response.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: I-I'm still overriding the city's broadcast power settings, and trying to expand its range. Maybe the landship's comms have a temporary malfunction... I'm doing my best to bring it back online!

a.text: Countdown
12 minutes, 57 seconds

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: I sense something peculiar, Dr. Kal'tsit.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: My mother... She's prepared incantations for every person dear to her heart. When they pass away, an elegy will play in our minds.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: I am still in good health at present, but...
Kal'tsit suddenly feels her blood run cold.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Even if Babel can capture Kazdel, it is bound to suffer grave losses.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Theresis was right. They can't unite. The division of the Sarkaz will be the new norm. Even given a long time, the Sarkaz are unable to go from a weak community to a world leader.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Most importantly, I pointed out another path to Theresis. His plans in Londinium will have a greater chance of success if the Sarkaz corrupt the land with Originium and destroy their enemies.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Isn't this a good thing?

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Such a determined race is now our followers. They will become the first brilliant bloodstain on the curtain of Originium as it spreads.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: That's right... We have no need to destroy them. No need to kill her.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: I... should use the 'Civilight Eterna'. I should try to guide its hidden functions, and then I wouldn't need to...

a.text: Searching internal array. Administrator permissions found.
Verified. Valid permissions.
Welcome, Dr. {@nickname}.
Entering <color=#FF4200>(Shipwide Defense System)</color>. Please confirm subsequent operation.
<color=#000000>Should I really let Babel continue their actions at this point?</color>

<color=#000000>Am I really going to renounce the sacrifices of billions of our people in the distant past, renounce their flesh and blood, ballads and songs, renounce the spark that they have waited for ten thousand years, renounce the Originium Project... all for a race who doesn't even know what the barrier is?</color>
<color=#000000>If, for the sake of Terra, Originium was stopped... If Theresa truly succeeds...</color>
<color=#000000>Then what have we been waiting for during the ten thousand years?</color>
Theresa and the races of Terra... Do they really not have even the slightest chance of success?
<color=#000000>They do not. How could I be so naive as to believe that? They are disunited, narrow-minded, undeveloped... An accident of life, a fortunate survival, that's all.</color>
All lives have the right to believe in their own hopes.
<color=#000000>But we have no time left.</color>
<color=#000000>It is right in front of us.</color>

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: ...Doctor?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Doctor! Can you hear me?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: That's strange. There are some... peculiarities in the Doctor's emotions.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Intense, and... shadowed.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Doctor, what exactly...?

a.text: Look.
There is the fiery light from the torn apart portal, like a smoldering gash across the sky.
Only after centuries will it dissipate into nothingness.
The stars are leaving from where we stand, like leaves trembling in the night.
Yet that ship from Talos-II still arrived at these rubble-strewn ruins.
That is life.
That is what we lost after our final day. That is the ancient ode to dispel any darkness.
To this day, we still do not understand how life appeared in this vast sea of stars.
But I think we should sing the praises of all that lives, and sing our own praises as well.
Originium is our song, the melody we offer to those who come after. Meddling with the evolution of civilization is arrogance, but I had no other choice.

steps.name: Oracle
steps.text: I have reneged on my promise. I have betrayed she who waited within time itself.

steps.name: Oracle
steps.text: It is because of the love I felt. Love for life. Love for existence. Love is eternally pure. It leaves me unthinking.

steps.name: Oracle
steps.text: Kal'tsit. Learn to love. Learn to believe. You have to think. Go and lead. Go and face the rolling stones that fall down the hills, screaming as they go.

steps.name: Oracle
steps.text: But in the end... I believe that you can learn to love. It is eternally pure. It is the child of every breathing creature. It is our nature.

steps.name: Oracle
steps.text: Go. Kal'tsit. Go see your surroundings, then see what lies by the most distant of mountains. Go seek what forms existence takes. I must go back.

steps.name: Oracle
steps.text: She had once taught me everything, once explored everything with fervor. But she has changed. She will not give me much time to act of my own accord.

steps.name: Oracle
steps.text: May we meet again, next time. We will meet again. Kal'tsit.

options: I believe in them. I believe in you, Kal'tsit.
Kal'tsit. I do not have much time left.
Search for traces of life. Search for hope and a future.
Kal'tsit... Go find your own answer.

a.text: Are you sure you want to disable the Shipwide Defense System?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Doctor—!

a.text: <color=#FF4200>(Restart boarding ID verification)</color> selected. Confirmed.
<color=#FF4200>(Restart Shipwide Communications Modules)</color> selected. Confirmed.
Loading...
Countdown has reached zero.

steps.text: The fluorescence of the control panel reflects off the Doctor's mask.
As the screen shuts down, the face beneath the mask is shrouded in darkness again.

a.text: How would you describe those who would pay any price to defend their people?
Some would call them heroes. Some would call them legends.
But such titles best take root in times of widespread war.
As a short era of peace begins, in the space of a night, those living legends will all be relegated to the land of stories and tales.
The children who hear such tales will ask: why have all the people who bear such grand titles disappeared?

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Because they chose to stay in the past.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: They had seen through their duty, and the new era they founded has no place for them.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Legends are forgotten. Heroes pass out of memory.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: And death arrives as it always does. None can escape it.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Duty spurs a hero to write an answer with death, to tread a muddy road.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: That is our fate.

a.text: The eve of Babel's departure from Kazdel

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Perhaps after many years, those who were left behind and vanished after we built our home will join us in our causes.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: They will bear a name wracked with infamy and settle this debate for us.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Perhaps.
The twins stand shoulder to shoulder.
By means of the memories stored within the Black Crown, they walk along the battlefield of yesteryear. Just as it was in the past.
The two mixed-blood Sarkaz step off the King's collapsed chariot, walking toward the battle...
Walking toward the future.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: So is this where we part ways?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: It is. Here, where we joined hands to change Kazdel, we part.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Even though you have been their King for so many years, at times... you are as you were back then.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Back when we were still young, I would often prick my fingers as I was sewing, staining the robes I would sell. Do you remember?

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Yes...

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: At the time, you were still a gloomy recruit, not allowed to wield a real sword, always dreaming of becoming a soldier of Kazdel one day.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: I, for my part, still did not understand why we had to hide wherever we went.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: But then came the day that the Royal Court took note of my work, and I got to meet Yliš. During that meeting, I summoned my courage to ask the King of Sarkaz—

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Where does our future lie?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: He had no answer, only bidding me to leave.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Only once I saw our defeated troops return to their homeland in ruins did I finally understand. The answer I sought could not be found in other lands, but 'here'—

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: —In 'Kazdel'.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Kazdel will only return to glory when one of us is gone.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: But the one who is destined to lose is you. Must you persist with this, Theresa?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: There are many by my side who support me.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Most Sarkaz who have suffered oppression and humiliation choose rebellion and violence.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: No matter if those who remain wish it or not, they will eventually be swept along by the tides and drawn into wars.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: But our generation must do something. I do not wish for this hatred in my hand to pass on to the next, where it will continue to fester and grow anew.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Even if I cannot change the future, the hope that will ignite the spark must be carried forward.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: I too must take charge of those who follow me.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: The cries answering the war do not come solely from Kazdel. There is no place for us anywhere in these lands.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: All I can do is give them a push.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: And so I will stay here. I choose to stay in the past, where the new generation of Sarkaz will one day look back.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Just like you.
